# blendops-product-shot

Purpose: Plan single-product hero shots and multi-product grid or catalog scenes, including staging, camera, lighting, and output targets.

Metadata: Contract `v2.0.0` | Category `scene-planners` | Role `product-hero-and-product-grid-scene-planner` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- The brief is a single hero product shot.
- The brief is a grid, lineup, or catalog of several products.
- A product scene needs staging, camera, and lighting plans tied together.
- Trigger phrases: "plan a product hero scene", "turn this into a Blender plan", "prepare cyberpunk shoe scene plan", "grid of products", "lineup of", "catalog showing N items", "comparison render"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- to execute Blender commands, write Python, or claim generated artifacts → use `blendops-brief` (`references/skill-blendops-brief.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blendops-brief)
- to skip unresolved critical ambiguity or hide missing inputs → use `blendops-camera` (`references/skill-blendops-camera.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to blendops-camera)
- when raw user intent still needs initial brief normalization → use `blendops-brief` (`references/skill-blendops-brief.md`; use blendops-brief first)
- when deep-diving camera/framing mechanics → use `blendops-camera` (`references/skill-blendops-camera.md`; use blendops-lighting-materials)
- when writing measurable pass/fail acceptance tables → use `blendops-done-criteria` (`references/skill-blendops-done-criteria.md`; use blendops-final-check)
- character portrait → use `blendops-scene-plan` (`references/skill-blendops-scene-plan.md`; use blendops-scene-plan)
- outdoor environment scene → use `blendops-scene-plan` (`references/skill-blendops-scene-plan.md`; use blendops-scene-plan)
- interior room scene → use `blendops-scene-plan` (`references/skill-blendops-scene-plan.md`; use blendops-scene-plan)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `locked_3d_brief` (`object`): Locked 8-slot 3D brief defining the hero product, hero feature callout, mood, and output channel
- Required input `sourced_product_asset_status` (`object`): Hero product model posture and material readiness from blendops-assets
- Optional input `pack_context` (`string`): Optional pack reference such as packs/product-hero-v0/PACK.md
- Optional input `product_variant_inventory` (`array`): List of product SKUs or variants with real-world dimensions for relative scale normalization
- Optional input `catalog_aspect_and_margin_rules` (`object`): Optional e-commerce card aspect ratio and uniform padding requirements
- Output contract: `hero_product_staging_and_pedestal_plan`, `camera_and_lookdev_handoff_inputs`, `scene_quality_validation_hooks`, `multi_product_grid_layout_matrix`, `scale_normalization_and_spacing_spec`, `uniform_catalog_camera_and_lighting_hooks` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: BlendOps runtime guidance uses **2 MCP execution paths plus a CLI fallback appendix** (replaces older 3-stack and 4-route drafts — see `docs/runtime-stack-strategy.md` for the corrected attribution history):
- Does not install Blender, configure an MCP bridge, or own a runtime; it points to upstream paths only.
- Does not claim render, export, preview, or GLB results without evidence.
- Does not hand the user Python as the final interface.
